title: Dehydration in children: grading and the three treatment plans
alt: Flowchart of WHO dehydration assessment. Two or more severe signs means Plan C: IV Ringer's lactate 100 mL/kg, 30 mL/kg in the first hour then 70 mL/kg over five hours, reassessing every 15 to 30 minutes. Two or more of the milder signs means Plan B: ORS 75 mL/kg over four hours, then reassess. Fewer signs means Plan A: extra fluids at home, ORS after each loose stool, continued feeding and zinc.
caption: Thresholds and regimens from the WHO/UNICEF diarrhoea guidance (IMCI and "The Treatment of Diarrhoea" manual).

nodes.text: Child with diarrhoea or vomiting: assess hydration
Two or more severe signs: lethargy, sunken eyes, drinks poorly, very slow skin pinch
Plan C: IV Ringer's lactate 100 mL/kg — 30 mL/kg in 1 hour, then 70 mL/kg in 5 hours
Older child: same volumes over 30 minutes then 2.5 hours
Reassess every 15–30 minutes; give ORS as soon as able; zinc for 10–14 days
Two or more of: restless, sunken eyes, thirsty, skin pinch slow
Plan B: ORS 75 mL/kg over 4 hours, small frequent sips; keep breastfeeding
Reassess at 4 hours: none → Plan A, some → repeat, severe → Plan C
Plan A: extra fluids at home, ORS after each loose stool, continue feeding, zinc
Return if blood in stool, drinking poorly, worsening, or no urine
